1.text:
“Alif-Lãm-Mĩm-Ṣãd” opens the surah as disconnected letters. One gloss uses the phrase “God knows best what He means by these letters”; another gives the wording “I am Allah Who knows best” and also keeps an oath reading. Two other explanations point back to an earlier explanation of disconnected letters. They do not give a word for each letter; the meaning remains with God. An overview of the surah links its subjects to the return to the Hereafter and prophethood, then to past prophets and their communities, along with their reward and punishment. Another note frames the Book as guidance for the few and a warning to those moving toward a grievous fate. These are subjects of the surah, not explanations of the four opening letters. The comments provide context for the chapter while leaving the meaning of the letters with God, as one gloss puts it.

**The letters, their readings, and the oath.**

Alif Lām Mīm Sād God knows best what He means by these letters. I am Allah Who knows best and is best; it is also said that this is an oath by which Allah swore. This surah begins with the disconnected letters, the explanation for which has already preceded in Surah Baqarah. We mentioned before the explanation of the letters [such as, Alif-Lam, that are in the beginning of some Surahs in the Qur'an].

**The surah’s subjects across its sections.**

An overview of the Surah shows that most of the subjects it deals with are related to Ma ad (Return to the Hereafter) and Risalah (Prophethood). The former appear from the beginning of the Surah upto approximately the end of the sixth section. Then, from the eighth to the twenty first sections, there is a detailed description of past prophets, events about their communities, their reward and punishment and the punishment which overtook them.

**Guidance, warning, truth, and substance.**

The Book of God is, in essence, a book of guidance. But as such it is of value only to the few who have kept their consciences alive. For the others it amounts only to a warning of the impending grievous fate towards which they are moving because of their arrogance. The preacher of truth is concerned to see that what he sees as the absolute truth is being rejected by the majority of the people who consider it a falsehood. What is paramount in his eyes is treated by people with unconcern, as if it had no substance, as if it were completely unreal.

2.text:
The verse first names what has been sent down: “This is a Book sent down to you, O Prophet.” The wording places the Book before the strain of carrying it, so its origin and its task are clear before the difficulty is named. “Do not let anxiety into your heart regarding it” speaks to the inner burden that can accompany a message rejected by its hearers. It does not change what the Book is or what it asks; it tells the Prophet not to be held back by the pressure around its delivery. The next words, “so with it you may warn the disbelievers,” give that delivery a purpose: the warning is carried through the Book, not made up apart from it. “And as a reminder to the believers” turns to another audience. The same Book warns those who reject it and renews the attention of those who believe. The line therefore joins reassurance with responsibility: the Prophet is not asked to control every response, but he is given a clear message to convey. Its closing phrase prepares for the next command, which tells people to follow what has been sent down and not to turn to other protectors. The emphasis is not on anxiety by itself, but on what the revealed words are for and how different hearers meet them. For those already believing, a reminder is useful because it brings the message back to mind; for those refusing it, the warning makes the consequence plain. Both purposes belong to the same Book. The letters at the start of the surah are followed by the plain name of the Book here, and the next verse turns from its purpose to the duty of following it.

**The revealed Book.**

This is a Book that is revealed to you — addressing the Prophet s — so let there be no inhibition no constraint in your breast because of it to convey it — for fear that you might be called a liar — that you may warn thereby li-tundhira ‘that you may warn’ is semantically connected to unzila ‘is revealed’ that is to say ‘it is revealed for the purposes of warning’ and as a reminder for those who believe in it. ((It is) a Scripture) this Scripture, i.e. the Qur'an (that is revealed unto thee (Muhammad) that Gabriel brought to you (so let there be no heaviness in thy heart) let there be no doubt in your heart (therefrom) i.e. there can be no doubt about the Qur'an being from Allah (that thou mayst warn thereby) that you may warn the people of Makkah through the Qur'an in order that they believe, (and (it is) a Reminder unto believers).

**The burden in the heart.**

Some commentators have said that haraj' or constraint on the heart' refers to the constraint experienced by the Holy Prophet who, because of his affectionate concern for people, felt pain when they would not believe despite having heard the Qur'an and its injunctions. To offset this constraint, the Holy Prophet has been told that the duty with which he has been obligated is simply to make the call and convey the message. (haraj) translated here as constraint' means that you should have no anguish or apprehension in conveying the Qur'an and its injunctions lest people belie it and hurt you.' (As reported from Abu Al- Aliyah - Mazhari) The hint given here is that Allah who has sent down this Book on you has also made arrangements that you shall remain protected and that takes care of any anguish on your part. The noble Qur’ān is a scripture revealed by Allah to you, O Prophet, so do not let there be any distress or doubt in your heart about it.

**The warning, truth, and substance.**

For the others it amounts only to a warning of the impending grievous fate towards which they are moving because of their arrogance. The preacher of truth is concerned to see that what he sees as the absolute truth is being rejected by the majority of the people who consider it a falsehood. What is paramount in his eyes is treated by people with unconcern, as if it had no substance, as if it were completely unreal. He revealed it to you to warn people by it and to be a proof, and to remind those who have faith through it, because it is they who benefit from being reminded.

3.text:
After naming the Book and its purpose, the verse turns from what was sent down to what people are to do with it. “Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord” makes the direction plain: the guidance is not something to be set aside when another voice is easier. “And do not take others as guardians besides Him” marks the alternative the verse refuses, a turn toward other protectors in place of the Lord. The command is not just to hear the words, but to keep to them, and the second phrase prevents a divided loyalty. “How seldom are you mindful” closes with a rebuke about remembering. It asks why people who have been shown what was sent down still act as if they had forgotten it. The verse links revelation to choice: people may accept or reject the message during their lives, yet the reminder calls them to bring what they know into their decisions now. It also moves the passage forward. The preceding verse described the Book as both warning and reminder; this verse explains the response expected from its hearers. The next verses turn to communities that failed to respond, showing that what is neglected in life does not disappear from the account. So the command to follow stands between a message given and the consequences of how people answer it. The verse speaks to all who hear, not just to the person first addressed, and it does not allow the hearer to treat another protector as a substitute for the instruction already sent down. Its closing words return to memory, making recollection practical in the choices that follow. The first phrase gives the direction, the next names what is to be left aside, and the last returns to memory. Read in order, the verse moves from revelation to obedience and then to the rebuke for forgetting. It does not leave the hearer with memory alone, because the command to follow comes before the words about remembering. The wording places other protectors besides the Lord and tells the hearer not to follow them. The warning and reminder in the verse before this one now become a direction for conduct.

**Following what was sent down.**

Say to them Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord namely the Qur’ān and do not follow do not take beside Him namely God in other words other than Him any patrons obeying them in disobedience of Him exalted be He. ((Saying): Follow that which is sent down unto you from your Lord) i.e. the Qur'an: uphold as lawful that which it makes lawful and unlawful that which it makes unlawful, (and follow) and worship (no protecting friends) idols as lords (beside Him. Little do you recollect) you do not take admonition neither much nor a little! (Follow what has been sent down unto you from your Lord) meaning, follow and imitate the unlettered Prophet , who brought you a Book that was revealed for you, from the Lord and master of everything.

**Following other protectors.**

(and follow not any Awliya', besides Him (Allah) meaning, do not disregard what the Messenger brought you and follow something else, for in this case, you will be deviating from Allah's judgment to the decision of someone else. Do not follow the desires of those you imagine to be friends and protectors amongst the devils or evil scholars, turning to them and leaving what was revealed to you because of your desires.

**Remembering, rejection, and truth.**

Little do you remember read tadhakkarūn or yadhakkarūn ‘little are you or they admonished’; the original tā’ of tatadhakkarūn has been assimilated with the dhāl; a variant reading has tadhkurūn; the mā of qalīlan mā ‘little’ is extra merely emphasising the ‘littleness’. Here everybody has the opportunity and the liberty to accept or reject the truth as he pleases, and even find clever words to justify his stand. As soon as the period of trial comes to an end, it will be revealed to all that the preacher’s words were based on eternal truths; that it was sheer bias and egotism on his opponents’ part which prevented them from seeing the Truth at the core of his arguments. It will become clear at that time that the arguments advanced by them to contradict the preacher’s words were simply a falsification of the facts and not a form of reasoning in any real sense. If you had remembered, you would not have preferred falsehood over the truth, and you would have followed what your Messenger came with, acting in obedience to it and leaving anything besides it.

4.text:
The verse opens by making the number of destroyed societies a question that points beyond any one town: “Imagine, how many societies We have destroyed!” It turns the listener toward repeated examples, not a single unexpected event. “Our torment took them by surprise, while sleeping, at night or midday” explains the turn. The communities did not take command of the moment or choose when to face it; the arrival is pictured as sudden. The final phrase sets two ordinary times side by side. Night is when people rest, while midday can also be a time of rest, so the warning reaches into hours when no one expects to be confronted. The verse does not describe a defense or a rescue by the powers they trusted. It brings the outcome forward and lets the next line give the words left to those who were overcome. The previous verses call the hearer to follow what was sent down and remind them of the result of refusing guidance. This verse makes that result visible through earlier societies, and the following verse gives their own short admission. The sequence moves from warning, to sudden punishment, to the confession that follows. In this way the question about how many is not a count to be worked out, but an invitation to think about how often a people has met the same end while feeling secure. The two times of day make the surprise plain, and the word societies broadens the lesson beyond one group. The sudden arrival matters because the people are shown at rest, not preparing to meet what comes. The two times do not set an hour for the hearer to expect; they show that punishment came both at night and in the middle of the day. A town’s confidence did not keep it safe. The number in the opening question remains broad, because the warning concerns a repeated outcome, not one group alone. The next line gives the words the people had left when that outcome reached them. The rest at night and midday makes the surprise part of the account rather than a detail about a single place.

**The number of destroyed towns.**

How many kam is predicative and is the direct object of the main verb ahlaknāhā ‘We have destroyed’ a city meaning its inhabitants have We destroyed have We willed its destruction! (How many a township) people of townships (have We destroyed) We tormented! How many cities Allah has destroyed through His punishment because they persisted in their disbelief and error! (And many a township did We destroy while they were given to wrongdoing, so that it lie in ruins (up to this day), and (many) a deserted well and lofty castle!)[22:45], and,.

**The night and the midday rest.**

So Our might Our chastisement came upon it at night or while they slept at noon qā’ilūn al-qaylūla is a rest taken halfway during the day even if it does not involve sleep in other words sometimes it came upon it at night and sometimes it came during the day. (Our torment came upon them by night or while they were taking their midday nap.) means, Allah's command, torment and vengeance came over them at night or while taking a nap in the middle of the day. Both of these times are periods of rest and leisure or heedlessness and amusement. (As a raid by night) or day, (or while they slept at noon, Our terror) Our punishment (came unto them). Allah sent His punishment down on them in their obliviousness at night or during the day: they could not do anything to avoid the punishment, and their false gods could do nothing to protect them from it.

**The world, truth, and untruth.**

In this world the importance of an individual is gauged by the material splendour surrounding him, and his ability to influence people with his impressive words, and thus have a massive following. Since the preacher is not generally in such a happy position, his word is valueless in the eyes of worldly people, while the words of his opponents, who bask in material grandeur have a greater impact. But when Doomsday uncovers all the facts, the position will be just the opposite. Now, all the weight will be on the side of the Truth: Untruth will be divested of all its arguments and will be rendered valueless.

5.text:
The line moves from the sudden arrival of the punishment to what its hearers could say afterward. “Their only cry” narrows the response to one statement, with no other plea placed beside it. “When overwhelmed by Our torment, was” locates that statement at the moment the punishment reaches them, not earlier when a warning could still be acted on. “We have indeed been wrongdoers” is the confession itself. They do not speak of a lack of signs or of another power that could protect them. The verse leaves the confession short, and the previous line explains why it comes only after the torment has arrived. The people now name their own wrong, but the words do not undo what has happened. In the surrounding passage, the Book has already been presented as warning and reminder, and the command was to follow what was sent down. This verse gives the consequence of ignoring that command from the side of those who are overtaken. The next line widens the account by placing both the communities and the messengers before questioning. The admission therefore belongs to a larger reckoning, where what was done and how the message was received are brought into view. The confession is brief because the line leaves no second plea beside it. Maʿārif’s earlier note concerns the Prophet’s pain when people heard the Qur’an and would not believe; here the same rejection reaches the moment of admitted wrong.

**The plea when the torment came.**

And their only plea their only words when Our might came upon them was to say ‘We were evildoers indeed’. (No cry did they utter when Our torment came upon them but this: "Verily, we were wrongdoers.") (No plea) words (had they, when Our terror) Our punishment which destroyed them (came unto them, save that they said: Lo! We were wrong-doers) idolaters. This means, when the torment came to them, their cry was that they admitted their sins and that they deserved to be punished.

**The wrong they admitted.**

(No plea) words (had they, when Our terror) Our punishment which destroyed them (came unto them, save that they said: Lo! We were wrong-doers) idolaters. All they could do when the punishment came down on them was to admit that they had done wrong through their disbelief in Allah. This means, when the torment came to them, their cry was that they admitted their sins and that they deserved to be punished.

**The plea at the time of torment.**

And their only plea their only words when Our might came upon them was to say ‘We were evildoers indeed’. (No plea) words (had they, when Our terror) Our punishment which destroyed them (came unto them, save that they said: Lo! We were wrong-doers) idolaters. (No cry did they utter when Our torment came upon them but this: "Verily, we were wrongdoers.") This means, when the torment came to them, their cry was that they admitted their sins and that they deserved to be punished.

To offset this constraint, the Holy Prophet has been told that the duty with which he has been obligated is simply to make the call and convey the message.

6.text:
The verse places two groups before a future questioning: “We will surely question those who received messengers and We will question the messengers themselves.” The first phrase points to the people who heard a message and must answer for how they received it. The second turns the question toward those who carried the message, so the record includes both the hearers and the ones sent to them. “We will surely question” is repeated in the meaning even as the subjects change, giving each group its own responsibility. The verse follows the account of communities that admitted wrongdoing only after punishment arrived. It now looks beyond that moment to the day when their response to messengers will be examined. At the same time, it does not collapse the two questions into one: people answer for their response, while messengers answer for conveying what they were sent with. The next verse promises a full account with knowledge, and that none of this happened in absence. So this line begins the scene of questioning, rather than giving every detail of the answers. The repeated question makes clear that the message and its reception both matter, while keeping the duty of the hearer distinct from the duty of the one sent.

**People and messengers before questioning.**

We shall question these people about their response to the messengers, (and verily We shall question the messengers) about their conveyance of the message. Allah will certainly question the communities He sent messengers to on the Day of Judgement: about how they received the messengers. Allah will question the nations, on the Day of Resurrection, how they responded to His Messengers and the Messages He sent them with.

**The messengers and their delivery.**

Then verily We shall question those to whom the Message was sent that is We shall question those communities about their response to the messengers and to what extent they implemented that which was conveyed to them; and We shall question the messengers about the conveying of that Message. He will also question the Messengers if they conveyed His Messages.

**The messengers and the questions asked.**

The statement: ‌ ‌ 6 in verse 6 refers to the day of Qiyamah when people will be asked by Allah how did they receive the messengers and Books sent to them by Him - and the messengers will be asked if they did convey to their communities the message and injunctions Allah had sent them with. Also, He will certainly question the messengers about whether they delivered what they were instructed to deliver, and how their communities responded to it.

7.text:
After saying that both the communities and the messengers will be questioned, the verse explains how the account will be given. “Then We will give them a full account with sure knowledge” points to a complete telling of what they did, not a partial recollection. This complete telling is not based on guesswork or on a report that might have been missed. The final phrase, “for We were never absent,” gives the reason the account can be complete: nothing was outside the knowledge of the One who was present when the messengers conveyed the message and when the people responded. The verse's order matters. It first promises a full account, then names the knowledge behind it, and closes by removing the possibility that some action escaped notice. The preceding verse asks both audiences about their part, while this one brings their whole story forward. The next verses describe the scales and the differing outcomes, so the account leads into a just weighing rather than ending with questioning alone. The line also answers any thought that an unseen or private action would be missing: what was done in public and what was hidden belongs to the same account. This is why the verse pairs a full telling with constant knowledge, and why the lack of absence is its final point. Neither time nor place could put a person's conduct beyond the account. The full telling is not just a list; it is an exact account of what was done.

**Knowledge and the facts brought to light.**

(Then verily We shall narrate unto them) inform them (with knowledge) with elucidation, (for verily We were not absent) from the conveyance of the messengers and the response of the people (when it came to pass). Allah will inform everyone about what they did in the world, through His knowledge, because He was always aware of whatever they did. But when Doomsday uncovers all the facts, the position will be just the opposite.

**The communities and messengers in the question.**

The statement: ‌ ‌ 6 in verse 6 refers to the day of Qiyamah when people will be asked by Allah how did they receive the messengers and Books sent to them by Him - and the messengers will be asked if they did convey to their communities the message and injunctions Allah had sent them with. Allah will question the nations, on the Day of Resurrection, how they responded to His Messengers and the Messages He sent them with.

**Nothing was absent from the account.**

(Then surely, We shall narrate unto them (their whole story) with knowledge, and indeed We have not been absent.) "The Book will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection and it will speak, disclosing what they used to do." Nothing is hidden from Him, and He was never, at any point, absent from them. (and indeed We have not been absent) meaning, On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will inform His servants about what they said and did, whether substantial or minor.

**Worldly judgment and the final truth.**

In this world the importance of an individual is gauged by the material splendour surrounding him, and his ability to influence people with his impressive words, and thus have a massive following. Since the preacher is not generally in such a happy position, his word is valueless in the eyes of worldly people, while the words of his opponents, who bask in material grandeur have a greater impact. Now, all the weight will be on the side of the Truth: Untruth will be divested of all its arguments and will be rendered valueless.

8.text:
This verse shifts from the full account to the measure by which deeds will be weighed. “The weighing on that Day will be just” states the standard before it names either outcome; no person is treated unfairly. “As for those whose scale will be heavy with good deeds” introduces one side of the result. The wording identifies what makes it heavy. “Only they will be successful” closes by naming success as the outcome for those whose deeds outweigh the other side. The line does not describe success as worldly status or as having more possessions. Its measure belongs to the Day when the whole account has been given. It follows the promise that every community and messenger will be questioned and that nothing was absent from the account. It then prepares for the next verse, which names the opposite scale and gives the light scale’s outcome. The two verses are placed together so that the justice of the weighing is heard before either result is described. The heavy scale is not a claim that a person was without fault; it is the stated side of a just comparison, with good deeds carrying weight. The phrase “on that Day” points back to the questioning and the full account, so the scale is part of one process. The ending does not leave the reader with a bare measurement; it names success as the result for those whose deeds weigh more. The verse gives the standard first, then moves from that standard to the first result, leaving the next line to state the other.

**A just weighing.**

The weighing of deeds or of the scrolls of these deeds shall be — in a balance that has a tongue and two palms as scales as reported in a hadīth — on that day that is on the day of the questioning mentioned namely the Day of Resurrection the true weighing the fair weighing al-haqq ‘the true’ is an adjectival qualification of al-wazn ‘the weighing’. Here, the hint given is that let no one be deceived by the idea that things which usually get to be weighed or measured are things having some weight or heaviness. Human deeds, good or bad, have no body or mass which could be weighed. (And the Weighing on that day is definite) so that man, all infatuated with the obvious, may not be able to deny the weighing of deeds in the Hereafter - which stands proved from the Holy Qur'an and is the collective belief of the Muslim Ummah. The weighing of what they did on the Day of Judgement will be with justice, with no one being wronged in the least.

**The things that are weighed.**

As for what will be placed on the Balance on the Day of Resurrection, it has been said that the deeds will be placed on it, even though they are not material objects. Allah will give these deeds physical weight on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that the Book of Records that contains the deeds will be weighed. A Hadith states that a man will be brought forth and ninety-nine scrolls containing errors and sins will be placed on one side of the balance each as long as the sight can reach. It is also possible to combine the meanings of these Ayat and Hadiths by stating that all this will truly occur, for sometimes the deeds will be weighed, sometimes the scrolls where they are recorded will be weighed, and sometimes those who performed the deeds will be weighed. Now, if Allah Almighty, the Maker of makers, in His perfect power, could weigh or measure human deeds - with or without a device - what is there in it which would make it to be something far out to believe? Leaving this aside for a moment, the Creator of the Universe does have the power to transform our deeds at some time into a material presence, even give it some shape or form (interesting that people would believe something like this happening in a Speilberg movie, yet squirm at the religious view of things as would come to pass).

**Heavy scales and the inward state.**

So, as for those whose scale (of good deeds) will be heavy, they will be the successful (by entering Paradise)And as for those whose scale will be light, they are those who will lose themselves for their wrongful behavior with Our Ayat. Those whose good actions weigh more than their bad actions have succeeded in reaching the goal and being saved from what they feared. The one whose scale-pan with good deeds is heavier will have his salvation while the one whose scale-pan with sins and evils is heavier will have his punishment. The weighing of deeds with the scales of self-purification is true, and the weighing of states with the scales of truthfulness is just. Hapless and deprived is he whose deeds are tainted with eye service and whose states are mixed with self-admiration, for in the station of the scales these states will have no value and those deeds will have no weight.

9.text:
The next line gives the other side of the weighing. “But those whose scale is light” turns from the successful to those whose deeds do not carry enough weight, and the contrast is signaled by the opening word. “They have doomed themselves for wrongfully denying Our signs” puts the loss on the people themselves; it is not described as a loss imposed without a reason. The ending names the action connected to that loss. The verse therefore does not leave the light scale as an unexplained result; it links it to denial. It follows the statement that the weighing is just, so the contrast between the scales is part of the same fair reckoning. The previous verse names success for those whose scale is heavy, and this verse names the self-loss of the other group. Together they set out two outcomes, not as a guess about anyone's present standing, but as a final result at the weighing. The next verses return from the Day of Judgment to the favors given in this world and the many who give little thanks; the contrast asks readers to notice how they respond before their deeds are weighed. The word “signs” gathers the message they had rejected, not one isolated mark. The scale is light because their actions and their denial meet in the same result, while the earlier line has named success on the other side.

**The light scale and its result.**

And as for those whose scales are light because of evil deeds those are the ones who have lost their souls by causing them to travel towards the Fire because they mistreated they knowingly denied Our signs. So, as for those whose scale (of good deeds) will be heavy, they will be the successful (by entering Paradise)And as for those whose scale will be light, they are those who will lose themselves for their wrongful behavior with Our Ayat.

**Those who lose themselves.**

(those are they who lose their souls) by being punished (because they disbelieved Our revelations) Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an. Those whose bad actions weigh more than their good actions are the people who have lost themselves, gaining their destruction on the Day of Judgement and being excluded from eternal bliss because of their rejection of Allah’s signs and verses. In the two verses the Tafsir of which you have just read through, sinners were warned against the disgrace on the plain of Resurrection and the Divine punishment that would come in its wake.

**Worldly standing, truth, and untruth.**

In this world the importance of an individual is gauged by the material splendour surrounding him, and his ability to influence people with his impressive words, and thus have a massive following. Since the preacher is not generally in such a happy position, his word is valueless in the eyes of worldly people, while the words of his opponents, who bask in material grandeur have a greater impact. But when Doomsday uncovers all the facts, the position will be just the opposite. Now, all the weight will be on the side of the Truth: Untruth will be divested of all its arguments and will be rendered valueless.

10.text:
The verse returns from the weighing to the life people now live. “We have indeed established you on earth and provided you with a means of livelihood” names the place where human life is set and what is needed to live there. The two phrases belong together: a place to live is accompanied by ways to seek food, drink, clothing, work, and other needs. The verse then marks the response with “Yet,” turning from what has been given to what people give back. “Yet you seldom give any thanks” does not deny that people receive these provisions; it shows their gratitude is small beside what they have received. The first-person wording keeps the gifts tied to their giver, while the closing phrase makes human forgetfulness the concern. The previous two verses described the scales of deeds on the Day of Judgment. This verse moves to present life and asks the reader to notice what choices are being made now, before the accounting. The following verses begin the story of Adam and Satan, which continues the warning about disobedience and ingratitude. So the line is both a reminder of provision and a test of how people respond to it. Its words do not limit livelihood to one kind of work or one kind of possession, but point to what sustains a life on earth. The final turn is not a small detail. It makes thanks the question raised by the verse and by the human story that follows.

**The earth and its comfort.**

Then comes the third verse which mentions the blessings of Allah Ta ala and persuades people to accept truth and act accordingly by suggesting that Allah has bestowed on them full ownership and control on the earth and has opened thousands of avenues of comfort for them. It is as if the Master of the Universe has made this whole earth and what it contains a giant warehouse of human needs and comforts, a most compre-hensive inventory of that inside it.

**Livelihood and life on earth.**

And We have given you power O Children of Adam in the earth and have appointed for you therein livelihoods ma‘āyish is the plural of ma‘īsha that is the means by which you are able to subsist; little qalīlan mā mā is to emphasise the ‘littleness’ thanks you show for this. (And We have given you (mankind) power in the earth, and appointed for you therein) in the earth (a livelihood) that from which you eat, drink and clothe yourselves. Allah certainly established you, O children of Adam, on the earth, and gave you the means of making a living.

**Sustenance and benefits.**

Allah reminds of His favor on His servants in that He made the earth a fixed place for dwelling, placed firm mountains and rivers on it and made homes and allowed them to utilize its benefits. Allah made the clouds work for them (bringing rain) so that they may produce their sustenance from them. He also created the ways and means of earnings, commercial activities and other professions. One who is short on sense and manners and does not know how to take things out from this warehouse, or does not understand how to use what he has taken out, he remains deprived of their benefits.

**Gratitude and forgetfulness.**

Whatever God has bestowed upon man in this world has been given for the purpose of eliciting his gratitude. But this is the very thing which man does not offer to his Lord. The reason for this is that Satan contrives to distort his feelings and steers him away from any expression of gratitude. You should be thankful to Allah for that, but you give little thanks. In short, Allah Ta ala has placed all that human beings need on and in this earth which demands that they should be grateful to Him all the time under all conditions. They would not take much time to forget the favours of their Creator and Master - only to return to the same world of things. So, at the end of the verse, it is in a mode of complaint that it was said: ‌ (Little you are receptive to advice).

11.text:
“Surely We created you” uses a plural address, though Adam is named in the next clause. “then shaped you” follows creation with form. Adam is the father of all mankind, and the plural therefore includes his offspring. The angels, not the offspring, are the ones who bow. “then said to the angels” names the group, and “Prostrate before Adam” gives the command. The glosses differ on the shaping. Some connect it to Adam's form and offspring in his line. One places the fashioning in wombs. “so they all did” is the angels' response. “but not Iblîs” makes the exception, and “who refused to prostrate with the others” states his refusal. The bow is an act of honor to Adam and a salutation. The plural and the angels' obedience are distinct points. The first includes Adam's offspring through their father. The other makes the angels' response plain. Another note warns Adam's children of Shaytan's enmity and of following his footsteps. A reflection on Adam's story places the test in the heart, where jealousy and pride develop. It also points to gratitude for what has been bestowed. The refusal stands beside the honor given to Adam, and the human story has a test of pride and gratitude. The beautiful faces, tall statures, two seeing eyes, two listening ears, and a speaking tongue are among His favors. He makes being from nonbeing, brings forth what is from what was not, and makes things newly from the outset. He is the maker of every being in a fitting way. He created the Adamites to manifest forgiveness and mercy, and the angels to manifest awe. To the dust-dwellers He showed only clemency and mercy. To the angels, only severity and all-compellingness.

**Adam as the father of all mankind.**

And We created you that is your father Adam then shaped you that is We shaped him with you deposited in his back then said to the angels ‘Prostrate yourselves before Adam!’ a prostration that is a bow of salutation. Therefore, the Ayah (7:11) refers to Adam, although Allah used the plural in this case, because Adam is the father of all mankind. But, since that was a favor given to the forefathers, and they are their very source, then the offspring have also been favored by it. O people, Allah created your father Adam, making him in the best of forms and the best of designs.

**Creation and the human form.**

" The wise Lord, the renowned and tremendous all-compeller, the enactor, the knowing keeper of ser vants, is reminding the children of Adam of His favors. He is saying, "I created you, and I sculpted your beautiful faces. I drew your tall statures and gave you two seeing eyes, two listening ears, and a speaking tongue. I am the Lord who makes being from nonbeing, who brings forth what is from what was not, and who makes things newly from the outset. The painter of faces is I, the adorner of beauties is I, the one who pairs everything with its companion is I, the maker of every being in a fitting way is I. I created heaven, earth, and the inanimate things to manifest power. I created Adam and the Adamites to manifest forgiveness and mercy. After Allah created Adam with His Hands from dried clay of altered mud and made him in the shape of a human being, He blew life into him and ordered the angels to prostrate before him, honoring Allah's glory and magnificence. (And We created you) from Adam and Adam is from dust, (then fashioned you) in wombs, and We fashioned Adam between Makkah and Ta'if, (then told the angels) who were on the earth: O people, Allah created your father Adam, making him in the best of forms and the best of designs.

**The angels' bow as honor.**

The angels all heard, obeyed and prostrated, but Iblis did not prostrate. Then He commanded the angels to bow down to him, honouring him, so they did so, all bowing down, except for Iblīs, the Satan, who refused to bow down out of pride and stubbornness. So they fell prostrate all save Iblīs the father of the jinn who was among the angels — he was not of those who make prostration. (Fall ye prostrate before Adam) a prostration of greeting! (And they fell prostrate, all save Iblis) their leader, (who was not of those who make prostration) to Adam. I created the angels, satans, and jinn to manifest awe. "For 700,000 years Gabriel, Michael, Seraphiel, the Cherubim, the Circlers, and the Row-keep ers circumambulated the Kaabah of All-Compellingness saying 'The Glorified! The Holy!' They never gained access to or recognized My names of love, loving kindness, and friendship. To the angels I showed only severity and all-compellingness. To the dust-dwellers I showed only clemency and mercy.

**Adam's children and Shaytan's enmity.**

Allah informs the Children of Adam about the honor of their father and the enmity of Shaytan, who still has envy for them and for their father Adam. So they should beware of him and not follow in his footsteps. Whatever God has bestowed upon man in this world has been given for the purpose of eliciting his gratitude. But this is the very thing which man does not offer to his Lord. The reason for this is that Satan contrives to distort his feelings and steers him away from any expression of gratitude. It becomes evident from the story of Adam and Satan what the real criterion is for the judgement of one’s case. Man is being judged at the point where feelings of jealousy and pride develop in the human heart. In this world of trial it happens again and again that one man rises above another; sometimes one man receives a greater share of wealth and honour as compared to his fellow men. Sometimes, in a deal between two persons, it happens that one of them considers his discharging of the other’s legitimate rights as degrading to himself. On all such occasions man is being judged whether he responds positively or reacts negatively. They never had the gall to claim friendship with Me, but I claimed friendship with the dust-dwellers: I derived several of My names from My friendship and loving kindness toward them: the Forgiving, the Loving, the Clement, the Ever-Merciful. " Among the angels, Gabriel was honored and foremost, and he was singled out for the special favors of proximity. He was standing constantly on the carpet of justice with the attribute of awe. He had never seen the carpet of bounty and expansive ness. Before Adam the Chosen came, there was no separation or union, no rejection or acceptance.

12.text:
“Allah asked, ‘What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?’ He replied” brings the command and Iblis's refusal into one question. It asks what held him back after the order to prostrate. “I am better than he is” is the claim of superiority and the excuse for refusing to bow. “You created me from fire and him from clay” makes his comparison. Fire is named for himself and clay for Adam. One gloss has fire devouring mud. The comparison is false. Mud has wisdom, forbearance, patience, and assurance, and is where plants grow and flourish. Fire burns and is reckless and hasty. The claim also looks only to the origin of creation, not to the honor bestowed on Adam, created with God's hand and given life. “I am better” makes superiority, rather than the command, the reason not to prostrate. Another reflection places jealousy and pride in the test and links humility with a different end. Denying another's superiority is also like denying God's decree. The origin of Adam leads to repentance, humbleness, obedience, and submission. Iblis's comparison leads to failure.

**The question about prostration.**

He exalted be He said ‘What prevented you from falling prostrate allā is made up of an-lā the lā being extra when I commanded you? (He said: What hindered thee) Allah said to Iblis: what prevents you (that thou didst not fall prostrate) to Adam (when I bade thee) to prostrate? (What prevented you (O Iblis) that you did not prostrate)[7: 12] meaning, what stopped and hindered you from prostrating after I ordered you to do so, according to Ibn Jarir. Allah asked Satan rebuking him: 'What stopped you from following My command to bow down to Adam?' Satan said: 'What prevented me is that I am better than Adam:

**Superiority, pride, and the failed response.**

(I am better than him (Adam), and this excuse is worse than the crime itself! Shaytan said that he did not obey Allah because he who is better cannot prostrate to he who is less. Shaytan, may Allah curse him, meant that he is better than Adam, "So how can You order me to prostrate before him? Shaytan made a false comparison when confronted by Allah's command,. On such occasions Satan stirs up feelings of jealousy and pride. ‘I am better,’ a man is not prepared to acknowledge the superiority of his brother. In the eyes of God, this amounts to treading the path of Satan. In such instances, one who treads the path of jealousy and pride makes himself deserving of the fate of hell, while one who remains humble proves that he deserves to find an abode in the gardens of Paradise. So, the admission of someone else’s superiority is in fact an admission of the propriety of God’s endowments. Thus, denying the superiority of a well-endowed person is like the denial of God’s own decree. Similarly, when one man yields to another on the basis of some truth, he is not bowing down before just some man but before God; he does so in response to God’s command and not because of the other’s personal superiority.

**Fire, clay, and the false comparison.**

((Iblis) said: I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire while him Thou didst create of mud) I am made of fire while he is made of mud, and fire devours mud. You created me from fire and Adam from mud, and fire is greater then mud.'. " Shaytan said that he is better than Adam because he was created from fire while, "You created him from clay, and fire is better. " The cursed one looked at the origin of creation not at the honor bestowed, that is, Allah creating Adam with His Hand and blowing life into him. His claim that the fire is more honored than mud was also false, because mud has the qualities of wisdom, forbearance, patience and assurance, mud is where plants grow, flourish, increase, and provide good. To the contrary, fire has the qualities of burning, recklessness and hastiness. Therefore, the origin of creation directed Shaytan to failure, while the origin of Adam led him to return to Allah with repentance, humbleness, obedience and submission to His command, admitting his error and seeking Allah's forgiveness and pardon for it. (The angels were created from light, Shaytan from a smokeless flame of fire, while Adam was created from what was described to you).

13.text:
“Allah said, ‘Then get down from Paradise’” opens with the command to descend. The comments differ on the place meant by “from here.” One keeps the Garden, while others give heaven or the angelic form. The translation names Paradise, but the glosses preserve these distinct readings. “It is not for you to be arrogant here” brings pride into the reason for the order. Iblis has defied the command and is told that arrogance has no place there. One commentary places this pride in an angelic form before the Children of Adam. Another connects the descent with disobedience. A further gloss has him leave the earth rather than the Garden. “So get out” follows the rebuke with another command. The order moves from the reason to its enforcement. “You are truly one of the disgraced” completes the reversal. The one who refused to bow because he claimed superiority is now humiliated and disgraced, the opposite of the arrogance he intended. Humiliation is the consequence of disobedience, not a claim that the command was unclear. This humiliation is just recompense for his ill intentions, the opposite of what he intended. The reflections on jealousy and pride place humility against the wish to be above others. Here that contrast ends in the status “disgraced.” The Garden, heaven, and angelic-form alternatives concern where the departure is from. The verse's own phrases about pride and disgrace remain clear.

**Paradise, heaven, and the angelic form.**

Said He ‘Then go down from it that is from the Garden — it is also said go down from the heavens — it is not right for you to show pride here so go forth out of it! It could also refer to particular status which he held in the utmost highs. (Then go down hence!) go down from heaven; it is also said this means: come out of angelic form. (It is not for thee) you ought not (to show pride here) demonstrate pride, in the form of an angel, to the Children of Adam, (so go forth!) leave your angelic form; it is also said that this means: go forth from the earth; (Lo! thou art of those degraded) you are of those who are humiliated in that you are punished. Allah told Satan: 'Go down from Paradise, because it is not appropriate for you to be proud in it; as it is a place for those who are good and pure-hearted.

**Arrogance and defiance of the command.**

(Get down from this) "because you defied My command and disobeyed Me. Get out, it is not for you to be arrogant here," in Paradise, according to the scholars of Tafsir. On such occasions Satan stirs up feelings of jealousy and pride. ‘I am better,’ a man is not prepared to acknowledge the superiority of his brother. In the eyes of God, this amounts to treading the path of Satan. Similarly, when one man yields to another on the basis of some truth, he is not bowing down before just some man but before God; he does so in response to God’s command and not because of the other’s personal superiority.

**Disgrace as the opposite of pride.**

Surely you are among the abased!’ the contemptible! (Get out, for you are of those humiliated and disgraced.) as just recompense for his ill intentions, by giving him the opposite of what he intended (arrogance). You are O Satan disgraced and humiliated, even though you consider yourself to be superior to Adam. In such instances, one who treads the path of jealousy and pride makes himself deserving of the fate of hell, while one who remains humble proves that he deserves to find an abode in the gardens of Paradise. So, the admission of someone else’s superiority is in fact an admission of the propriety of God’s endowments. Thus, denying the superiority of a well-endowed person is like the denial of God’s own decree.

14.text:
“He appealed, ‘Then delay my end until the Day of their resurrection’” records the request, not the answer. Iblis asks for respite until the people are raised. The glosses give the wording as a request for reprieve or relief. The day he names is the Resurrection, not an unspecified pause. The following verse gives the response, so the request and the actual term of respite should not be merged. One reading takes his prayer as answered until the Resurrection. The appointed time mentioned elsewhere places the end of the grant earlier, at the first blowing of the Horn. These readings concern how long he is granted respite, not what he asks for here. This verse marks the request. The limit on the grant is taken up in the answer.

**Respite requested until the Day.**

This is when the cursed one remembered and asked for respite until the Day of Judgment,. Said he ‘Reprieve me postpone my affair until the day when they people are resurrected’. (He said: Reprieve me) give me respite (till the day when they are raised) from the graves-accursed not wanting to die. Satan asked Allah: 'O my Lord, give me relief until the Day of Rising, so that I could tempt and misguide whomever of the children of Adam I am able to tempt.'. He asked for a lease of life until the day of Resurrection. But, what is not stated in this verse clearly is whether the giving of respite mentioned here is until the Resurrection as asked by Iblis, or is for some other duration.

**The requested day and the appointed time.**

He was given respite till a particular time and not till the day of Resurrection or Qiyamah. Allah Ta ala did not give respite to Iblis till the day of Resurrection, instead, He has given him respite till a day the time of which is appointed and that is the day when the Horn will be blown the first time and whoever there is in the heavens or the earth shall be stunned, and dead.

**Respite and divine decree.**

The words in which Allah Ta ala answered the prayer, as they appear in this verse, are no more than: ‌ (Respite is given to you). From these words, given the nature of the question and the answer, it can be understood that this respite was given until the Resurrection as asked by him. Allah gave Shaytan what he asked for out of His wisdom, being His decision and decree, that is never prevented or resisted. Surely, none can avert His decision, and He is swift in reckoning.

15.text:
“Allah said, ‘You are delayed ˹until the appointed Day˺’” gives the answer to the request, but it does not simply repeat the day Iblis asked for. He asked to be reprieved until the Resurrection. The verse names an appointed time for the respite granted. The words can be understood as granting his request through the Resurrection, but the other verse about an appointed time restricts that reading. The limit is the first blowing of the Horn. The concise glosses likewise give the first trumpet blast or the time until the trumpet is blown. The grant remains within God's wisdom and decree. The request belongs to the previous verse. This one gives an answer but not the length Iblis wanted.

**Respite until the Resurrection.**

He asked for a lease of life until the day of Resurrection. The words in which Allah Ta ala answered the prayer, as they appear in this verse, are no more than: ‌ (Respite is given to you). From these words, given the nature of the question and the answer, it can be understood that this respite was given until the Resurrection as asked by him. But, what is not stated in this verse clearly is whether the giving of respite mentioned here is until the Resurrection as asked by Iblis, or is for some other duration.

**The first trumpet blast and its time.**

You are of those reprieved’ — in another verse it is said until the day of an appointed time Q. 3881 that is until the time of the first blast of the Trumpet. (Lo! thou art of those reprieved) you are given respite until the trumpet is blown. Allah told Satan: 'You are O Satan given respite till the first blast of the trumpet when all created beings die, and the Creator alone remains.'. He was given respite till a particular time and not till the day of Resurrection or Qiyamah.

**Respite and Allah's decision.**

Allah Ta ala did not give respite to Iblis till the day of Resurrection, instead, He has given him respite till a day the time of which is appointed and that is the day when the Horn will be blown the first time and whoever there is in the heavens or the earth shall be stunned, and dead. Allah gave Shaytan what he asked for out of His wisdom, being His decision and decree, that is never prevented or resisted. Surely, none can avert His decision, and He is swift in reckoning.

16.text:
“He said, ‘For leaving me to stray I will lie in ambush for them on Your Straight Path’” is Iblis's own speech. The opening bā is read as an oath, whose response is Iblis's vow to sit in ambush. Other glosses give the words as “as You sent me astray” or “as You caused my ruin,” and another connects the error to his failure to follow the command to bow down to Adam. These glosses remain Iblis's own words, not a separate account of the command. He turns from the charge to a plan. “I will lie in ambush for them on Your Straight Path.” The straight path leads to God and is the way of truth and safety. The servants created from Adam's offspring are the people in the ambush, and the straight path is the way of truth and safety that Iblis wants them not to follow. The intended ambush is against worshipping God alone, because the straight path leads to God and to safety. The ambush is a plan to misguide people from worshipping God alone, to discourage them from good, and to lure them toward evil. The reflection on “I am better” links jealousy and pride with refusing to acknowledge another's superiority. Humility is the other response. The earlier refusal to honor Adam now becomes a threat against his offspring, a movement from pride to active misguidance. The verse keeps the threat in Iblis's own speech and names the path he intends to obstruct.

**Error, ruin, and the command.**

("Because You have 'Aghwaytani', surely, I will sit in wait against them (human beings) on Your straight path.") meaning, as You have sent me astray. Ibn 'Abbas said that 'Aghwaytani' means, "Misguided me. " Others said, "As You caused my ruin, I will sit in wait for Your servants whom You will create from the offspring of the one you expelled me for. Satan said: 'Because You have made me fall into error through not following Your command to bow down to Adam, I will surely sit in wait for the children of Adam upon Your straight path, to turn them away and mislead them from it, just as I was misled through not bowing down to Adam.'.

**The oath and the Straight Path.**

Said he ‘Now because You have sent me astray fa-bi-mā aghwaytanī means bi-ighwā’ik ‘for Your sending me astray’ the bā’ is for oaths and the response of the oath is the following verily I shall sit in ambush for them that is for the Children of Adam on Your straight path that is on the path that leads to You. I (Iblis) will misguide them from this path so that they do not worship You Alone, because You sent me astray. Shaytan discourages the people from the path of good and lures them to the path of evil.

**Awe in the divine presence.**

The place where Iblis dared to speak was in the Most August conceivable Presence of the Master of all Honour where the awe and majesty of the occasion would not allow even angels and prophets and messengers to breathe. How did he do that? Ulama say that this was a somber and highly cutting manifestation of the Divine wrath that, because of the rejection of Iblis, his view was so obstructed (hijab) that he became blind to the grandeur and awe of Allah Ta ala and irreverence came down to settle on him all over.

**Jealousy, pride, and superiority.**

On such occasions Satan stirs up feelings of jealousy and pride. ‘I am better,’ a man is not prepared to acknowledge the superiority of his brother. In the eyes of God, this amounts to treading the path of Satan. In such instances, one who treads the path of jealousy and pride makes himself deserving of the fate of hell, while one who remains humble proves that he deserves to find an abode in the gardens of Paradise. Thus, denying the superiority of a well-endowed person is like the denial of God’s own decree. Similarly, when one man yields to another on the basis of some truth, he is not bowing down before just some man but before God; he does so in response to God’s command and not because of the other’s personal superiority.

17.text:
“I will approach them from their front, their back, their right, their left” gathers the plan into four sides. The commentaries caution that these do not set limits, but mean Iblis will come from all sides and directions. The approaches have different targets. Doubt about the Hereafter comes from before, attachment to worldly life from behind, confusion in religion from the right, and sins or pleasures from the left. The verse gives the directions as ways to divert people, not a literal map with an uncovered side. The omission of an approach from above is connected with mercy descending from above. Another account preserves a prayer seeking protection from every direction and above. “and then You will find most of them ungrateful” turns from the plan to its expected result. “Most” matters. The verse gives Iblis's prediction, not a claim that every person will follow him. Thankfulness is glossed as belief. Another rendering pairs denial with ingratitude, and another specifies those who single God out in worship. The plan and its expected result stay distinct. The verse records Iblis's threat, not that all are overcome.

**From all sides, not from above.**

In the present verse , Iblis is said to have identified four sides from which he planned to mislead the children of 'Adam, that is, the front, the rear and the right and the left. But, the purpose here is not to set up any limits. Instead, the sense is that this will be from all sides and directions. Therefore, the probability of his leading people astray from above and beneath the feet does not contradict it. Similarly, the saying of the Hadith that - Shaytan can enter the human body and move through the arteries and veins of blood and take command of the whole body - is also not contradictory to this. Ibn ‘Abbās said ‘However he cannot come upon them from above lest he come between the servant and the mercy of God exalted be He’. "He did not say that he will come from above them, because the mercy descends from above." 'Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas said,. This is why there is a Hadith that encourages seeking refuge with Allah from the lures of Shaytan from all directions. (O Allah! I ask You for well-being in this life and the Hereafter. O Allah! I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, life, family and wealth. O Allah! Cover my errors and reassure me in times of difficulty. O Allah! Protect me from before me, from behind me, from my right, from my left and from above me. I seek refuge with Your greatness from being killed from below me.)"

**Before, behind, and every direction.**

(Then I shall come upon them from before them) with regard to the Hereafter that there is no hell, Paradise, resurrection or reckoning (and from behind them) that the life of this world is everlasting and I shall bid them to amass and withhold out of stinginess and I will order them to commit corruption (and from their right hands) vis-�-vis the religion: 'I will surely come to them from every direction, causing them to neglect the Afterlife, and desire the life of this world, giving them doubts, and making their low desires seem beautiful to them. (Then I will come to them from before them) Raising doubts in them concerning their Hereafter,. (and (from) behind them), making them more eager for this life,. Shaytan discourages the people from the path of good and lures them to the path of evil.

**Belief, worship, and thankfulness.**

I shall confuse those who are guided until they leave the guidance, and I shall make it seem fair to those who are misguided such that they remain misguided (and from their left hands) as regard pleasures and delights, (and Thou wilt not find most of them) all of them (beholden (unto Thee) believers in You. (and You will not find most of them to be thankful.) "means, those who single Him out [in worship]. " When Shaytan said this, it was a guess and an assumption on his part. And You will not find O my Lord most of them thankful to You, because of the denial and ingratitude I will lead them to.

18.text:
“Allah said, ‘Get out of Paradise’” states the removal again, with the translation naming the place from which Iblis is expelled. The first saying, “So go, you are of the low,” is perhaps a proposal. This second saying, “Get out of here, condemned,” is its implementation. “You are disgraced and rejected” brings together abasement and banishment. The glosses range from despised and belittled to being removed from mercy or far from good. The words do not need to be reduced to one English synonym. The verse then continues, “I will certainly fill up Hell with you and your followers all together.” The followers are not every person without distinction. They are those who follow and obey him, going against the command. One gloss speaks of disbelievers among the jinn and human beings, while another extends the address to Iblis's seed and people. The sources differ in their precise grouping, but the threat concerns those who follow his way. The moral reflection connects this end with jealousy and pride, and contrasts the proud person's fate with the humble person's Paradise. The warning is twofold. The adversary is cast out, and Hell is threatened for those who follow him.

**Degraded, banished, and removed.**

Allah emphasized His cursing, expelling, banishing and turning Shaytan away from the uppermost heights, saying;. Ibn Jarir said, "As for Madh'um, it is disgraced. " And he said, "Madhur is the distanced, that is, he is banished and expelled." 'Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd bin Aslam said, "We do not know of any who is Madh'uh and Madhmum except for one. " Ar-Rabi' bin Anas said that 'Madh'um' means banished, while, 'Madhura' means belittled. (He said: Go forth from hence, degraded) rebuked, (banished) far from good. Allah said: 'Go down from Paradise O Satan, humiliated and removed from My mercy.

**The followers and the filling of Hell.**

As for those of them of people who follow you la-man ‘as for those who’ the lām is for inceptiveness; or it is for introducing the oath which is the following I shall assuredly fill Hell with all of you’ that is with you through your seed and with people — herein in this address those present have predominance over those absent this last sentence of the verse expresses the sense of ‘the requital’ suggested in the conditional man ‘who’ in other words ‘whoever follows you then I shall punish him’. Whoever of them (mankind) will follow you, then surely, I will fill Hell with you all. (Whoever of them (mankind) will follow you, then surely, I will fill Hell with you all.) This is similar to. (As for such of them) from the jinn and humans (as follow thee) obey you, (surely I will fill hell with all of you) of the disbelievers among the jinn and humans. I will certainly fill Hell with you and all those who follow and obey you and go against My command.

**The command, first saying, and implementation.**

In the cited verses (13 18), the Shaytan has been commanded to leave the heavens twice. First, when it was said: ‌ ‌ (So, go. You are of the low.) and then, when it was said: ‌ ‌ (Get out of here, condemned ...). Here, the first saying is perhaps a proposal while the other is its implementation. Similarly, when one man yields to another on the basis of some truth, he is not bowing down before just some man but before God; he does so in response to God’s command and not because of the other’s personal superiority.

**Pride, superiority, and the fate of the humble.**

On such occasions Satan stirs up feelings of jealousy and pride. ‘I am better,’ a man is not prepared to acknowledge the superiority of his brother. In the eyes of God, this amounts to treading the path of Satan. In such instances, one who treads the path of jealousy and pride makes himself deserving of the fate of hell, while one who remains humble proves that he deserves to find an abode in the gardens of Paradise. So, the admission of someone else’s superiority is in fact an admission of the propriety of God’s endowments. Thus, denying the superiority of a well-endowed person is like the denial of God’s own decree.

19.text:
“Allah said, ‘O Adam’” opens with the person whom the instruction names. “Live with your wife in Paradise and eat from wherever you please” places Adam and his spouse among the innumerable good things of Paradise, with freedom to use them. “but do not approach this tree” places one prohibited thing among countless good things. The translation calls it only “this tree.” One gloss has wheat, another the tree of knowledge. Because those names differ, neither should be carried into the verse as a certain identification. “or else you will be wrongdoers” names the consequence attached to approaching it. The prohibition is narrow beside the broad permission. The verse's command is not to approach the tree, and its stated outcome is wrongdoing. Adam's name and clay also open a reflection on his human nature. He was created from the surface of the earth and drawn from every region. The clay is sweet and briny, soft and hard. In this spiritual account, the mixture is linked to diverse natures among his children. His root is shown so that he would not see generosity as coming from himself. Eminence lies in nurture, not soil. In the Ayaz example, treasures and robes of honor are set beside an old patched cloak. When he looks at it, he sees his helplessness and abasement. This reflection on clay and measure sits alongside the command without replacing it. The prohibition also becomes a vantage point in the commentary on the deception that follows. Satan uses the one prohibited thing as an opening, magnifying its importance and placing it before the many legitimate gifts. The temptation in the next verse grows from that emphasis. Here the permission, the one forbidden thing, and the consequence remain the main parts of the instruction.

**Paradise, good things, and one prohibited thing.**

Paradise with all its vast expanses was open to Adam and his spouse. There were innumerable types of good things in it. And they had all the freedom to use them in whatever manner they liked. In the midst of countless permitted things, they were prohibited the use of only one thing. Allah states that He allowed Adam and his wife to dwell in Paradise and to eat from all of its fruits, except one tree.

**Wheat or the tree of knowledge.**

And He said ‘O Adam dwell you anta this is reiterated in order to emphasise the subject of the verb uskun ‘dwell’ and to supplement to it what follows and your wife Eve read Hawwā’ in the Garden and eat from whence you will but do not come near this tree to eat of it — and this was wheat — lest you become evildoers’. (And (unto man): O Adam! Dwell thou and thy wife) Eve (in the Garden and eat from whence) in Paradise (ye will) and whenever you will, (but come not nigh this tree) do not eat from this tree: the tree of knowledge (lest ye become wrong-doers) lest you become of those who harm themselves.

**Adam's clay and the natures of his children.**

In other words, he was extracted from every region sweet and briny, soft and hard. In Adam's clay were salty and sweet, coarse and soft, so the natures of his children became diverse. Among them are both sweet-tempered and bad-tempered, open and closed, generous and stingy, easy-going and difficult, black and white. Elsewhere He said, "He created man from dried clay, like pottery" [55:14]. Pottery is dried clay that gives off sound and is full of noise. In other words, the Adamite is noisy, his head full of tumult and turmoil, attached to talking. Elsewhere He said, "from clinging clay" [37:11], from a clay that is sticky, clings to every thing, and mixes with everyone. Elsewhere He said, "from fetid mud" [15:26], a clay that is dark and black.

**Adam's clay, root, and measure.**

He was called Adam because he was created from the surface [adīm] of the earth, drawn from every region. Thus He said, "[We created man] from an extraction of clay" [23:12]. Thus He taught him his measure so that he would not transgress his stage. He was shown his own root so that, if he should see generosity, he would not see it from himself. He would know that eminence lies in nurture [tarbiya], not in soil [turba]. He saw all the property, blessings, gold, silver, jewels, multicolored silks, and robes of honor that MaḤmūd had given to him and bestowed upon him. In a corner he saw an old cloak made of patches of cloth hanging from a nail. " Ayāz answered, "This one is me in all my helplessness and abasement. All that beauty, adorn ment, and all that exaltedness and delight are you. When I look at this, I see my own incapacity and know my own worth. When I look at that, I see you and know that it belongs to you, so I am delighted and lift my head.

**The prohibition and Satan's strategy.**

Satan used this prohibition as a vantage point from which to attack them. He incited them to wrongdoing by saying that the thing from which they were kept away was the most important thing in Paradise, the whole secret of holiness and eternity was hidden therein. Adam and his spouse were influenced by Satan’s continuous urging and finally ate the fruit of the forbidden tree. But, when they did this, the result was entirely the opposite of what they had expected. This disobedience of theirs removed the cloak of safety from their bodies. They became absolutely helpless in a world where they had had every convenience and total safety. This indicates the special weapon used by Satan to deceive man into distancing himself from God’s grace and succour. His strategy was to belittle in the eyes of man the extensive world of legitimate gifts from God and to inflate the importance of the few prohibited things, by presenting them in an attractive light, all the while reassuring man of the immense advantages concealed within them. In performing this task, Satan treats everybody according to his tastes and circumstances.

“Then Satan tempted them in order to expose what was hidden of their nakedness, He said” joins the whisper to its purpose. The hidden thing is described in more than one way. A gloss speaks of the shameful parts concealed by an attire of light, while another distinguishes what appeared to Adam and his spouse from what appeared to others. The wording keeps the exposure within their encounter. The verse does not describe an audience seeing them. “Your Lord has forbidden this tree to you only to prevent you from becoming angels or immortals” is the argument Satan gives them. It is his account of the prohibition, not the reason given by God. This is Satan's lie. Satan promises that eating will make them angels or give them immortality. These are Satan's words, not God's promise. One reading emphasizes becoming angels. Another emphasizes life forever in Paradise. The quoted “only” sharpens the lure by turning a command into a supposed barrier to a great benefit. This tactic works against the context of the prior permission. Adam and his wife were in Paradise with many good things and freedom to use them, with one tree prohibited. Satan used the one prohibition as a vantage point, made it look like the most important thing, and inflated what he presented as its hidden advantage. He belittles the legitimate gifts while making the prohibited thing attractive. The promised holiness and eternity are what Satan inflates, while the result removes the safety and convenience they had enjoyed. The next verses show the result. Adam and his spouse are influenced by continuous urging, they eat, and what follows is the opposite of what they expected. When they eat, the result is opposite to their expected gain. They are not made angels or immortals. The cloak of safety is removed from their bodies, and they become helpless in a world where every convenience had been theirs. A spiritual reflection describes the whisper's allowance as a mark of solicitude and generosity even after their sin. It does not make Satan's words true. The reflections also distinguish Adam's appetite from Iblis's pride. Adam slipped through appetite, while Iblis fell through pride. Pride is worse than satisfying appetite. Appetite leaves room for pardon, while faith is lost when the sin comes from pride. The verse itself contains the whisper, its purpose, and the false promise. These remain Satan's words. Satan's strategy adapts to people's tastes and circumstances.
